metadata.disclaimer: These recipes are designed for Crohn's disease patients. Always consult your healthcare provider or dietitian before making dietary changes.
metadata.notes: All recipes tagged by recovery phase, dietary restrictions, and key nutrients. Phase safety indicates minimum recovery phase where recipe is appropriate.

recipes.name: Plain White Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Simple, easy-to-digest white rice. The safest staple during a flare.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Combine rice, water, and salt in a pot. Bring to boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 18 minutes.
Remove from heat, keep covered 5 minutes. Fluff with fork.
recipes.crohns_notes: White rice is one of the most universally tolerated foods during a Crohn's flare. Low residue, low fiber, easy to digest.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Safe at all stages post-resection. Low fat content means no bile acid concerns.

recipes.name: Simple Chicken and Rice
recipes.description: Tender poached chicken breast over white rice. Gentle protein and carbs.

ingredients.notes: check broth for onion/garlic if low-FODMAP

instructions: Bring 2 cups broth/water to a gentle simmer in a pot.
Add chicken breasts, cover, and poach on low heat for 20-25 minutes until internal temp reaches 165°F.
While chicken cooks, prepare rice with remaining 1 cup liquid + 1 cup water.
Remove chicken, let rest 5 minutes, then slice or shred.
Serve chicken over rice.
recipes.crohns_notes: Poaching keeps chicken tender and easy to digest — much gentler than grilling or frying. Avoid adding spices during a flare.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Excellent post-resection meal. Low fat, high protein for healing. B12 from chicken supports ileal resection patients.

recipes.name: Banana Oatmeal
recipes.description: Creamy oatmeal with ripe mashed banana. Gentle soluble fiber and natural sweetness.

ingredients.notes: must be ripe (yellow with brown spots)

instructions: Combine oats and water in a pot. Bring to a simmer.
Cook 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until creamy.
Mash banana and stir into oatmeal.
Add pinch of salt. Serve warm.
recipes.crohns_notes: Oats are soluble fiber — generally well tolerated. Ripe banana is low-FODMAP at 1 medium. Unripe/green banana is high in resistant starch and may cause issues.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Good source of soluble fiber for stool consistency. Keep to 1/2 cup oats to stay in safe fiber range early post-resection.

recipes.name: Scrambled Eggs
recipes.description: Soft, creamy scrambled eggs. Quick protein that's easy on the gut.
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl, whisk until uniform.
Melt butter in nonstick pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in eggs, stir gently with spatula as they set.
Remove from heat while still slightly wet — they'll finish cooking from residual heat.
Season with salt.
recipes.crohns_notes: Eggs are one of the most tolerated protein sources for Crohn's patients. Cook soft/scrambled rather than fried for easier digestion.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Excellent B12 and vitamin D source. Fat is moderate — if bile acid diarrhea is an issue, use 2 eggs instead of 3 or cook with spray oil.

recipes.name: Applesauce
recipes.description: Homemade smooth applesauce. Gentle, soothing, pectin-rich.
instructions: Peel, core, and chop apples into small chunks.
Place in pot with water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, simmer 15-20 minutes until very soft.
Mash with a fork or blend until smooth.
Stir in cinnamon if using. Serve warm or chilled.
recipes.crohns_notes: Cooked, peeled apples are well tolerated. Pectin (soluble fiber) can help firm loose stools. Keep to 1/2 cup serving to stay low-FODMAP.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Safe post-resection. Pectin may help manage loose stools common after resection.

recipes.name: White Toast with Smooth Peanut Butter
recipes.description: Simple toast with a thin layer of smooth peanut butter. Quick energy and protein.

ingredients.notes: sourdough is also good — lower FODMAP than regular wheat
smooth only — no chunky. Check label for no added sugar alcohols
ingredients.substitution: smooth almond butter (limit 1 tbsp for low-FODMAP)

instructions: Toast bread to desired level.
Spread thin layer of smooth peanut butter.
Cut in half if easier to eat in small bites.
recipes.crohns_notes: Smooth peanut butter at 2 tbsp is low-FODMAP. Stick to 1 tbsp if cautious. White bread is low residue — choose over whole wheat during flares.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Keep peanut butter to 1 tbsp to limit fat if bile acid malabsorption is an issue.

recipes.name: Chicken Bone Broth
recipes.description: Rich, healing bone broth. Sip throughout the day for hydration and nutrients.

ingredients.notes: from a rotisserie chicken works great
remove before serving — just for flavor

instructions: Place bones in a large pot. Add water and vinegar.
Add carrots and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a very low simmer.
Simmer 4-6 hours (or 2 hours in pressure cooker).
Strain through fine mesh strainer. Discard solids.
Cool and refrigerate. Skim fat layer off top before reheating.
Store in fridge 5 days or freeze in portions.
recipes.crohns_notes: Bone broth provides easily absorbed minerals and amino acids (glutamine, glycine, proline) that may support gut lining repair. Skim fat off top for low-fat version.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Excellent for hydration and electrolyte replacement post-resection. Skim fat off top to prevent bile acid-related diarrhea.

recipes.name: Mashed Potatoes
recipes.description: Smooth, creamy mashed potatoes. Comfort food that's easy to digest.
instructions: Peel potatoes and cut into 1-inch chunks.
Boil in salted water until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain well. Return to pot.
Add butter and warm milk. Mash until smooth.
Season with salt. Do not over-mix or they'll get gluey.
recipes.crohns_notes: Peeled, well-cooked potatoes are low residue and well tolerated. Using lactose-free milk avoids dairy issues. Potatoes are a good potassium source.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Good for electrolyte replenishment (potassium). Moderate fat — reduce butter if bile acid diarrhea is active.

recipes.name: Baked Salmon with White Rice
recipes.description: Simple baked salmon fillet over rice. Omega-3 rich, anti-inflammatory protein.

ingredients.substitution: cod or tilapia for lower fat

instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Place salmon on lined baking sheet. Brush with olive oil, season with salt.
Bake 12-15 minutes until salmon flakes easily.
Squeeze lemon juice over top if desired.
Serve over white rice.
recipes.crohns_notes: Salmon is one of the best anti-inflammatory proteins for Crohn's due to omega-3 fatty acids. Baking is gentler than frying.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Fat is moderate at 14g — if bile acid diarrhea is active, switch to cod or tilapia (2-3g fat) instead. Excellent B12 source for ileal resection patients.

recipes.name: Oral Rehydration Solution
recipes.description: Homemade electrolyte drink for dehydration during flares or post-surgery.

ingredients.notes: regular white sugar — needed for sodium-glucose co-transport

instructions: Add sugar and salt to water. Stir until fully dissolved.
Add lemon juice if desired.
Sip throughout the day — do not chug.
Keep refrigerated. Make fresh daily.
recipes.crohns_notes: Based on WHO ORS formula. The sugar-salt ratio is critical — sugar enables sodium absorption via co-transport mechanism. Plain water alone can actually worsen dehydration in severe diarrhea.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Essential post-resection, especially with shortened bowel. Sip between meals, not during meals, to slow transit time.

recipes.name: Turkey and Rice Soup
recipes.description: Clear, soothing soup with tender turkey and soft rice.

ingredients.notes: check for onion/garlic — use FODMAP-safe brand

instructions: Brown turkey in a large pot over medium heat, breaking into small pieces.
Add broth, carrots, rice, salt, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook 20-25 minutes until rice and carrots are very soft.
Taste and adjust salt.
recipes.crohns_notes: Soup is easier to digest than solid meals. Well-cooked carrots are low residue and provide vitamin A. The broth helps with hydration.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Ideal post-resection meal — low fat, high protein, good hydration, soft texture. Carrots provide vitamin A (fat-soluble vitamin that may be depleted).

recipes.name: Banana Smoothie
recipes.description: Simple 3-ingredient smoothie. Creamy, filling, and gentle.
instructions: Add all ingredients to blender.
Blend until smooth.
Pour and serve immediately.
recipes.crohns_notes: Smoothies are easier to digest than whole foods during a flare. Ripe banana is low-FODMAP. Lactose-free dairy avoids common trigger.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Good for calorie intake when appetite is poor post-surgery. Low fat. Calcium from yogurt is important after resection.

recipes.name: Herb-Baked Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Juicy baked chicken thighs with dried herbs. More flavorful than breast, still easy to digest.

ingredients.notes: remove skin after cooking to reduce fat if needed

instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Pat chicken dry. Rub with olive oil.
Mix herbs, salt, and paprika. Sprinkle over chicken.
Place on baking sheet. Bake 30-35 minutes until internal temp 175°F.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.crohns_notes: Dark meat chicken has more iron and zinc than breast. Dried herbs are generally well tolerated. Remove skin to cut fat by ~40%.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Remove skin to reduce fat if bile acid diarrhea is active. Excellent iron and B12 content for resection patients.

recipes.name: Pasta with Garlic-Infused Oil
recipes.description: Simple pasta with FODMAP-safe garlic flavor. No actual garlic pieces.

ingredients.notes: FODMAPs are water-soluble, not fat-soluble — the oil has garlic flavor without the FODMAPs
ingredients.substitution: plain olive oil + pinch of asafoetida

ingredients.notes: aged parmesan is low-FODMAP (lactose is consumed during aging)

instructions: Cook pasta in salted boiling water per package directions.
Drain, reserving 1/4 cup pasta water.
Toss pasta with garlic-infused oil and a splash of pasta water.
Top with parmesan and basil.
Season with salt.
recipes.crohns_notes: Garlic-infused oil is a game-changer for low-FODMAP cooking — you get garlic flavor without the fructans that cause gas and bloating. Never use actual garlic pieces.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Moderate fat from olive oil. Enriched pasta provides iron and B vitamins. Good calorie-dense option for weight maintenance.

recipes.name: Tuna Salad Lettuce Wraps
recipes.description: Light tuna salad wrapped in butter lettuce. High protein, low residue.

ingredients.notes: finely diced — low-FODMAP at this amount

instructions: Drain tuna and place in a bowl.
Add mayo, celery, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Mix well, breaking up tuna chunks.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and wrap.
recipes.crohns_notes: Canned tuna is a convenient protein source rich in B12 and omega-3. Butter lettuce is one of the most gentle greens for Crohn's patients.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Good B12 source for ileal resection. Moderate fat — use light mayo if bile acid diarrhea is present.

recipes.name: Steamed White Fish with Zucchini
recipes.description: Delicate steamed fish with soft zucchini. Very low fat, very gentle.
instructions: Set up steamer basket over simmering water.
Place zucchini slices in steamer first. Steam 3 minutes.
Add fish on top. Season with salt.
Cover and steam 8-10 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Transfer to plate. Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice.
Garnish with dill if using.
recipes.crohns_notes: White fish is one of the lowest-fat protein options. Steaming preserves nutrients without adding oil. Peeled zucchini is very well tolerated — one of the first vegetables to reintroduce.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Ideal post-resection protein — extremely low fat (3.5g) means zero bile acid concern. High B12. Peeled zucchini is safe early post-resection.

recipes.name: Sweet Potato Mash
recipes.description: Smooth mashed sweet potato. Nutrient-dense comfort food.

ingredients.notes: peeled and cubed — low-FODMAP at 1/2 cup serving

instructions: Peel and cube sweet potatoes.
Boil in water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain. Add butter, salt, and cinnamon.
Mash until smooth.
recipes.crohns_notes: Sweet potato is rich in vitamin A (beta-carotene) which is important for gut lining health. Keep serving to 1/2 cup to stay low-FODMAP. Mashing makes it easier to digest than baked.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Excellent vitamin A source — this fat-soluble vitamin is often depleted post-resection. Mash with a small amount of fat (butter) to aid absorption.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Chicken Bowl
recipes.description: Grilled chicken with roasted vegetables, olives, and feta over rice. Anti-inflammatory and satisfying.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Toss zucchini and bell pepper with 1 tbsp olive oil, oregano, and salt. Spread on baking sheet.
Season chicken with remaining olive oil and salt. Place on same sheet.
Roast 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through and veggies are tender.
Slice chicken. Serve over rice with roasted vegetables.
Top with olives, feta, and lemon juice.
recipes.crohns_notes: Mediterranean diet has the strongest evidence for anti-inflammatory benefits in Crohn's. Olive oil, olives, and vegetables are the foundation. Only attempt during stable remission.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Fat is moderate at 20g — split into smaller portions if bile acid diarrhea is active. Peel zucchini and deseed pepper if still in early reintroduction.

recipes.name: Ginger-Turmeric Rice with Chicken
recipes.description: Anti-inflammatory spiced rice bowl. Ginger and turmeric are natural soothers.
instructions: Cook rice with turmeric and a pinch of salt per package directions.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add ginger, cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken cubes and carrots. Cook 8-10 minutes until chicken is done.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken and carrots over turmeric rice.
recipes.crohns_notes: Turmeric (curcumin) has evidence for reducing intestinal inflammation in IBD. Black pepper increases curcumin absorption by 2000%. Ginger is a natural anti-nausea agent.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Low fat, high protein — ideal post-resection. Turmeric's anti-inflammatory properties may help at the surgical site. Carrots provide vitamin A.

recipes.name: Egg Fried Rice
recipes.description: Quick fried rice with eggs and vegetables. A satisfying one-pan meal.

ingredients.notes: green parts are low-FODMAP — white parts are high

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over high heat.
Add carrots, stir-fry 2 minutes.
Push carrots to one side, pour beaten eggs into empty side. Scramble until just set.
Add cold rice. Stir-fry 3-4 minutes, breaking up any clumps.
Add soy sauce, toss to combine.
Remove from heat. Drizzle sesame oil, top with green onion tops.
recipes.crohns_notes: Green parts of green onions are FODMAP-safe — only the white bulb contains fructans. This is a great trick for adding onion-like flavor. Well-cooked carrots are safe.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Moderate fat — manageable for most post-resection patients. Good B12 from eggs.

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Baked Cod
recipes.description: Light, flaky cod with herbs and lemon. Extremely low fat, high protein.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Place cod on lined baking sheet. Brush with olive oil.
Season with salt. Lay lemon slices on top.
Bake 12-15 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
recipes.crohns_notes: Cod has only 1g fat per 3 oz serving — one of the leanest proteins available. Perfect when you need protein without fat-related symptoms.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Best protein choice for bile acid malabsorption patients. Virtually no fat to worry about.

recipes.name: Butternut Squash Soup
recipes.description: Creamy, velvety squash soup. Naturally sweet, packed with vitamin A.

ingredients.notes: peeled, seeded, cubed — low-FODMAP at 1/3 cup

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add squash, carrots, and ginger. Cook 3 minutes.
Add broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer 25 minutes until very soft.
Blend with immersion blender until smooth.
Season with salt and nutmeg.
Serve warm. Can freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
recipes.crohns_notes: Butternut squash is extremely rich in beta-carotene (vitamin A). Blending makes fiber content easier to digest. Keep serving to 1/3 cup squash per serving for strict low-FODMAP.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Excellent source of vitamin A (fat-soluble — the olive oil helps absorption). The smooth, blended texture is ideal post-resection.

recipes.name: Turkey Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
recipes.description: Tender turkey meatballs in a gentle tomato sauce. Kid-friendly, crowd-pleasing.
instructions: Mix turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, basil, oregano, and salt. Form into 16 small meatballs.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Brown meatballs on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Pour crushed tomatoes over meatballs.
Simmer covered 20 minutes until meatballs are cooked through.
Serve over white rice or gluten-free pasta.
recipes.crohns_notes: Small meatballs are easier to digest than a large piece of meat. Tomato sauce is generally well tolerated in remission — some patients need to avoid during flare due to acidity.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Good protein and iron. Moderate fat. Tomato sauce provides vitamin C which aids iron absorption.

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Banana Overnight Oats
recipes.description: No-cook breakfast you prep the night before. Grab and go.

ingredients.notes: small amount for omega-3 — skip if stricture risk

instructions: Combine oats, milk, peanut butter, chia seeds, and maple syrup in a jar.
Stir well. Top with banana slices.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours).
Eat cold or microwave 1-2 minutes.
recipes.crohns_notes: Overnight oats are softer than cooked oats — some patients find them easier to digest. The fiber is mostly soluble. Only for remission — too high fiber for flare.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Higher fiber (7g) — only appropriate once fully past reintroduction phase. Skip chia seeds if any stricture concern at anastomosis site.

recipes.name: Chicken Stir-Fry with Rice Noodles
recipes.description: Quick stir-fry with tender chicken and soft vegetables over rice noodles.
instructions: Cook rice noodles per package directions. Drain.
Heat garlic-infused oil in wok or large pan over high heat.
Add chicken, stir-fry 4-5 minutes until browned.
Add ginger, zucchini, bell pepper. Stir-fry 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Add soy sauce and noodles. Toss to combine.
Drizzle sesame oil. Serve immediately.
recipes.crohns_notes: Rice noodles are gluten-free and very easy to digest. Garlic-infused oil gives great flavor without FODMAP triggers. Cook vegetables until soft, not crunchy.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Cook vegetables very well — avoid al dente. Fat is moderate. Good protein for healing.

recipes.name: Greek-Style Chicken Salad
recipes.description: Chopped chicken salad with cucumber, olives, and feta. Refreshing and satisfying.
instructions: Combine chicken, cucumber, tomatoes, olives, and feta in a bowl.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, and salt.
Toss salad with dressing.
Serve over rice or with gluten-free pita.
recipes.crohns_notes: Mediterranean ingredients (olive oil, olives) are anti-inflammatory. Peeled cucumber is very well tolerated. Only for stable remission due to raw vegetables.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Higher fat (22g) — eat as a half portion if bile acid diarrhea is active, or reduce olive oil.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Glazed salmon over rice with steamed vegetables. Restaurant-quality at home.

ingredients.notes: well cooked — heads only, not stems for lower FODMAP

instructions: Mix soy sauce, maple syrup, ginger, and rice vinegar for teriyaki glaze.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Brush pan with oil.
Cook salmon skin-side up 4 minutes. Flip.
Pour teriyaki glaze over salmon. Cook 4-5 more minutes, spooning glaze over.
Steam broccoli until very tender (5-7 minutes).
Serve salmon over rice with broccoli. Drizzle remaining glaze. Top with sesame seeds.
recipes.crohns_notes: Homemade teriyaki avoids hidden garlic/onion found in bottled sauces. Broccoli heads are lower FODMAP than stems — cook very soft. Maple syrup is FODMAP-safe unlike honey.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Great omega-3 and B12 content. Cook broccoli very well. Skip sesame seeds if anastomosis stricture risk.

recipes.name: Protein Recovery Smoothie
recipes.description: High-protein smoothie for post-surgery recovery or low appetite days.

ingredients.notes: isolate has almost no lactose — check label for sugar alcohols

instructions: Add all ingredients to blender.
Blend until smooth.
Drink slowly — sipping is better than chugging for absorption.
recipes.crohns_notes: Whey protein isolate is generally well tolerated even by lactose-intolerant patients — the lactose is removed during processing. Check label to confirm <1g lactose per scoop.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Excellent for maintaining protein intake when appetite is poor post-surgery. Liquid nutrition absorbs more easily with shortened bowel.

recipes.name: Anti-Inflammatory Berry Smoothie
recipes.description: Blueberry and spinach smoothie with anti-inflammatory ginger. Nutrient powerhouse.

ingredients.notes: frozen — low-FODMAP at this serving size
mild flavor blends in — high oxalate, so limit if kidney stone history

instructions: Add all ingredients to blender.
Blend on high until completely smooth.
Serve immediately.
recipes.crohns_notes: Blueberries are rich in anthocyanins with anti-inflammatory properties. Blending spinach breaks down fiber, making it easier to digest than eating raw. Only for stable remission.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Caution with spinach if you have kidney stone history post-resection (high oxalate). Otherwise, a great way to get iron and vitamin A.

recipes.name: Ginger Peach Smoothie
recipes.description: Soothing peach and ginger smoothie. Great when nausea is present.

ingredients.notes: in juice, drained — canned is lower FODMAP than fresh
optional — honey is HIGH FODMAP in large amounts, keep to 1 tsp max

instructions: Add all ingredients to blender.
Blend until smooth.
Serve immediately. Sip slowly for nausea.
recipes.crohns_notes: Ginger is one of the best natural anti-nausea remedies. Canned peaches are lower FODMAP than fresh because excess fructose leaches into the syrup/juice. Always drain.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Very low fat, gentle on the system. Good for days when solid food feels like too much.

recipes.name: Carrot Ginger Soup
recipes.description: Silky smooth carrot soup with warming ginger. Vitamin A powerhouse.
instructions: Heat olive oil in pot. Add carrots and ginger, cook 3 minutes.
Add broth and salt. Bring to boil, simmer 20-25 minutes until carrots are very soft.
Blend until silky smooth with immersion blender.
Stir in coconut cream if using.
Taste and adjust salt.
recipes.crohns_notes: Carrots are one of the richest sources of beta-carotene (vitamin A). Blending eliminates fiber concerns. Ginger is anti-inflammatory and anti-nausea.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Outstanding vitamin A source — critical post-resection as this fat-soluble vitamin is often depleted. The small amount of olive oil aids absorption.

recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.description: Classic comfort chicken noodle soup. Healing, hydrating, homey.

ingredients.notes: egg noodles, orzo, or small shells

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot. Add carrots and celery, cook 3 minutes.
Add broth and thyme. Bring to a boil.
Add chicken breasts. Simmer 15 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken, shred with two forks.
Add pasta to broth. Cook per package directions.
Return shredded chicken to pot. Season with salt.
Serve hot.
recipes.crohns_notes: The classic sick-day soup. Broth provides hydration and electrolytes. Small pasta and well-cooked vegetables keep it low residue. Comforting during flares.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Excellent post-resection meal — hydrating broth, easily digestible protein, low fat. Cook vegetables until very soft.

recipes.name: Potato Leek Soup (FODMAP-Safe Version)
recipes.description: Creamy potato soup using only the green parts of leeks for FODMAP safety.

ingredients.notes: ONLY the dark green tops — white parts are HIGH FODMAP

instructions: Slice green parts of leeks. Wash thoroughly (leeks trap dirt).
Melt butter in pot. Sauté leek greens 3 minutes.
Add potatoes and broth. Bring to boil.
Simmer 20 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
For chunkier version, blend only half and stir back in.
recipes.crohns_notes: Classic potato leek soup adapted for low-FODMAP. The green parts of leeks have the flavor without the fructans concentrated in the white bulb. Great hack for onion-family flavor.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Smooth texture is ideal post-resection. Good potassium source. Low fat.

recipes.name: Rice Cakes with Peanut Butter and Banana
recipes.description: Crunchy rice cake topped with smooth PB and banana slices. Quick energy.

ingredients.notes: check label — no added flavoring with garlic/onion

instructions: Spread peanut butter on rice cakes.
Top with banana slices.
recipes.crohns_notes: Quick, portable snack. Rice cakes are very low residue. Peanut butter at 1 tbsp is low-FODMAP.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Good snack between meals — small, frequent eating is better post-resection than 3 big meals.

recipes.name: Hard-Boiled Eggs
recipes.description: Simple, portable protein. Make a batch for the week.
instructions: Place eggs in pot. Cover with cold water by 1 inch.
Bring to a rolling boil.
Remove from heat, cover, let sit 12 minutes.
Transfer to ice water bath for 5 minutes.
Peel and season with salt. Store unpeeled in fridge up to 7 days.
recipes.crohns_notes: Eggs are consistently one of the best-tolerated protein sources for Crohn's patients. Batch cook on Sunday for the whole week.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Great B12 and vitamin D source. Portable for snacking between meals — important for the small, frequent eating pattern recommended post-resection.

recipes.name: Lactose-Free Yogurt with Maple Drizzle
recipes.description: Creamy yogurt with a touch of maple sweetness. Probiotics and protein.

ingredients.notes: plain, not flavored — check for inulin/chicory in ingredients

instructions: Spoon yogurt into bowl.
Drizzle with maple syrup.
Eat slowly.
recipes.crohns_notes: Lactose-free yogurt still contains live cultures (probiotics). Many Crohn's patients tolerate this even during flares. Always check ingredient list for added inulin or chicory root — many yogurts add these as 'prebiotics' which are high FODMAP.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Important calcium source post-resection. Probiotics may help gut health. Easy to eat when appetite is low.

recipes.name: Homemade Protein Bites
recipes.description: No-bake energy bites with oats, peanut butter, and maple syrup. Make a batch for the week.
instructions: Mix all ingredients in a bowl until combined.
If too dry, add a splash of milk. If too wet, add more oats.
Roll into 12 balls (about 1 tbsp each).
Place on lined plate/sheet. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Store in airtight container in fridge for up to 1 week.
recipes.crohns_notes: Small, calorie-dense bites are great for snacking between meals. Keep to 1-2 at a time. Only for remission — oats + peanut butter may be too much fiber during a flare.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Good for maintaining calorie intake between smaller meals. Low fat per bite. Avoid if stricture risk — oats can clump.

recipes.name: Turkey Burger Patties (No Bun)
recipes.description: Lean turkey burgers seasoned with herbs. High protein, low fat.
instructions: Mix turkey with oregano, basil, and salt.
Form into 4 patties about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Cook patties 5-6 minutes per side until internal temp reaches 165°F.
Serve with mashed potatoes, rice, or in a lettuce wrap.
recipes.crohns_notes: Bunless burgers avoid gluten and excess fiber. Lean turkey is one of the gentlest meats. Pair with a tolerated carb for a complete meal.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Excellent high-protein, moderate-fat option. Rich in zinc and B12 which are commonly depleted post-resection.

recipes.name: Tofu Scramble
recipes.description: Plant-based protein scramble with turmeric. Looks like eggs, packed with nutrients.

ingredients.notes: drained and pressed — firm tofu is low-FODMAP
wilts down — high oxalate so limit if kidney stone history
optional — adds cheesy flavor and B12

instructions: Drain tofu, wrap in clean towel, press to remove excess water.
Heat garlic-infused oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat.
Crumble tofu into pan with your hands.
Add turmeric, salt, and pepper. Stir to coat.
Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add spinach, cook 2 more minutes until wilted.
Top with nutritional yeast if using.
recipes.crohns_notes: Firm tofu is low-FODMAP (silken tofu is higher FODMAP). Nutritional yeast is fortified with B12 — great for plant-based patients. Only attempt during stable remission due to spinach.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Good calcium source (tofu is calcium-set). Skip spinach if kidney stone history post-ileal resection. Nutritional yeast provides B12.

recipes.name: Shrimp and Rice
recipes.description: Quick sautéed shrimp over white rice with lemon. Fast, high-protein, very low fat.
instructions: Pat shrimp dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Add shrimp in a single layer. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until pink.
Squeeze lemon juice over shrimp. Season with salt.
Serve over rice, garnished with parsley.
recipes.crohns_notes: Shrimp is very low fat and cooks in minutes. Excellent B12 source. Some patients react to shellfish — introduce carefully.
recipes.post_resection_notes: One of the best post-resection proteins — extremely lean, high B12, high selenium. Low fat means no bile acid concerns.

recipes.name: Beef and Vegetable Stew (Low-Residue)
recipes.description: Tender beef stew with well-cooked carrots and potatoes. B12 and iron rich.
instructions: Pat beef dry. Season with salt.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high. Brown beef in batches, 3-4 minutes. Set aside.
Add broth to pot, scraping up browned bits.
Return beef. Add tomato paste and thyme. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to low simmer, cover. Cook 1 hour.
Add potatoes and carrots. Cook 30 more minutes until everything is very tender.
Season to taste.
recipes.crohns_notes: Beef is the richest food source of B12 and heme iron (best absorbed form). Long, slow cooking makes the meat very tender and easy to digest. Only for stable remission.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Top B12 food source — critical for ileal resection patients. Heme iron from beef absorbs better than plant iron. Cook until meat is fall-apart tender.

recipes.name: Pan-Seared Chicken Livers
recipes.description: Quick-cooked chicken livers. The single richest food source of iron and B12.
instructions: Pat livers dry. Season with salt.
Melt butter in pan over medium-high heat.
Add livers. Cook 3-4 minutes per side until browned outside but still slightly pink inside.
Add thyme in last minute.
Squeeze lemon over. Serve immediately.
Pair with white rice or mashed potatoes.
recipes.crohns_notes: 3 oz of chicken liver provides 280% daily B12 and 65% daily iron. If you can tolerate it, eating liver once a week can significantly help prevent deficiencies. Not for everyone — strong flavor.
recipes.post_resection_notes: The most nutrient-dense food for post-resection patients. Incredibly rich in B12, iron, vitamin A, and folate — all nutrients depleted by resection. Even once every 2 weeks makes a difference.

recipes.name: Steamed Tilapia with Lemon and Dill
recipes.description: Ultra-lean white fish with herbs. Under 2g of fat per serving.
instructions: Set up steamer basket over simmering water.
Season fish with salt. Place lemon slices and dill on top.
Steam 8-10 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Serve immediately.
recipes.crohns_notes: Tilapia has only 2g fat per serving — one of the leanest proteins available. Perfect when you need maximum protein with minimum digestive burden.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Best choice for severe bile acid malabsorption. Almost no fat means zero bile acid concern. Pair with white rice for a complete meal.

recipes.name: Batch Chicken and Rice Meal Prep
recipes.description: Make 5 lunches in one session. Simple, reliable, always ready.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Season chicken with olive oil, oregano, paprika, and salt.
Bake 25-30 minutes until internal temp 165°F.
While chicken bakes, cook rice per package directions.
Steam carrots until tender.
Let chicken rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Divide into 5 meal prep containers: chicken + rice + carrots.
Refrigerate up to 5 days. Reheat in microwave.
recipes.crohns_notes: Meal prep is a game-changer for Crohn's patients — when you're exhausted, a healthy meal is already ready. No decision fatigue, no temptation to eat something risky.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Perfect post-resection meal prep. Low fat, high protein, well-cooked vegetables. Having meals ready prevents resorting to processed foods when energy is low.

recipes.name: French Toast (Low-FODMAP)
recipes.description: Classic French toast made FODMAP-safe. A weekend treat.

ingredients.notes: sourdough fermentation reduces FODMAPs in wheat

instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, cinnamon, and vanilla in a shallow dish.
Melt butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat.
Dip each bread slice in egg mixture, coating both sides.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Serve with maple syrup and sliced banana if desired.
recipes.crohns_notes: Sourdough bread is lower FODMAP than regular wheat bread because the fermentation process breaks down fructans. This is a great trick for enjoying bread on low-FODMAP.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Moderate fat — adjust butter amount if needed. Good calorie-dense breakfast for maintaining weight post-resection.

recipes.name: Cream of Rice with Cinnamon
recipes.description: Smooth, warm cereal that's extremely gentle. The safest breakfast during a flare.
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a small pot.
Slowly stir in cream of rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cook 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat. Stir in cinnamon, maple syrup, and salt.
recipes.crohns_notes: Cream of rice has virtually zero fiber — it's one of the gentlest foods you can eat during a severe flare. Many hospitals serve this post-surgery.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Perfect for early post-surgery days when transitioning from liquids to soft foods. Essentially predigested carbohydrates.

recipes.name: One-Pot Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.description: Everything on one sheet pan. Minimal cleanup when energy is low.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Toss potatoes and carrots with 1 tbsp olive oil and half the seasonings on a sheet pan.
Season chicken with remaining oil and seasonings. Nestle among vegetables.
Bake 35-40 minutes until chicken reaches 175°F and vegetables are tender.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.crohns_notes: One-pan meals are perfect for low-energy days — minimal prep, minimal cleanup. Drumsticks are more forgiving than breast (harder to overcook).
recipes.post_resection_notes: Remove chicken skin to reduce fat if bile acid diarrhea is active. Well-cooked root vegetables are easily digestible.

recipes.name: Risotto with Parmesan
recipes.description: Creamy, comforting risotto. The slow stirring is meditative, the result is delicious.

ingredients.notes: warm — keep simmering in separate pot

instructions: Keep broth warm in a separate pot over low heat.
Heat garlic-infused oil and 1 tbsp butter in a wide pan over medium heat.
Add rice. Toast 2 minutes, stirring until edges are translucent.
Add wine if using. Stir until absorbed.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring frequently. Wait until each addition is mostly absorbed before adding the next.
Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining butter and parmesan.
Season with salt. Serve immediately.
recipes.crohns_notes: Risotto is essentially a porridge of rice — very easy to digest. Parmesan is aged and naturally low in lactose. Garlic-infused oil adds flavor without FODMAP triggers.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Low fiber, easy to digest. Parmesan provides calcium. Moderate fat — reduce butter if needed.

recipes.name: Miso-Glazed Chicken
recipes.description: Umami-rich miso chicken. Simple but tastes restaurant-quality.

ingredients.notes: white/shiro miso is milder — check for added garlic

instructions: Mix miso, maple syrup, rice vinegar, and sesame oil into a glaze.
Spread half the glaze on chicken breasts.
Preheat broiler. Place chicken on lined baking sheet.
Broil 6-8 minutes per side, brushing with remaining glaze when you flip.
Let rest 5 minutes. Slice and serve over rice.
recipes.crohns_notes: Miso is fermented soybean paste — a natural probiotic. White miso is milder and usually better tolerated than red miso. Rich umami flavor without needing garlic or onion.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Low fat. Fermented foods like miso may support gut microbiome recovery post-surgery. Higher sodium — good for electrolyte replacement but watch if on low-sodium diet.

recipes.name: Mac and Cheese (Crohn's-Safe Version)
recipes.description: Creamy mac and cheese made with lactose-free milk and aged cheddar. Comfort food you can actually eat.
instructions: Cook pasta per package directions. Drain.
In the same pot, melt butter over medium heat.
Whisk in flour. Cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in milk. Stir until thickened, about 3 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in cheese, salt, and mustard powder until melted and smooth.
Add pasta back to pot. Stir to coat.
recipes.crohns_notes: The secret: aged cheddar is naturally very low in lactose because bacteria consume the lactose during aging. Combined with lactose-free milk, this is genuinely safe for most lactose-intolerant patients.
recipes.post_resection_notes: Higher fat (18g) — eat a smaller portion if bile acid diarrhea is active. Excellent calcium source which is critical post-resection.
